changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.42[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Usenet[/COLOR]
-New: release details in the sources list, as icons at the right end of each NZB card: file type (MKV, RAR, 7Z, RAR>ISO, 7Z>RAR>ISO, a Blu-ray disc, locked, PAR2), grabs, indexers (xN), age and a score from 0 to 100 (green, amber or grey by how likely it is to play). NZBs of the same resolution are sorted by that score. It can be turned off in Settings > Usenet.
-New: releases that hold a RAR set inside a 7z or inside another RAR now play, including disc images and Blu-ray folders inside them.
-New: posts with scrambled file names are named from their own PAR2 index and opened again. The names are kept for the next time.
-New: subtitle files posted with the release (.srt, .ass, .ssa, .vtt) are offered to Kodi as subtitle tracks.
-New: indexer searches ask for a second page when the first comes back full, so releases past the first hundred are no longer lost.
-Fixed: a whole Blu-ray posted as loose files played only one piece of the film. It now plays complete, and its playlists are read over several connections, so it starts sooner.
-Fixed: grabs and the real post date were missing for movie and text searches.
-A disc image without a readable playlist plays its largest clip instead of failing, and the health check of a loose Blu-ray samples all its pieces.
-Source Info no longer shows your indexer API key or Easynews login in the link.
[COLOR fffdb515]TMDb[/COLOR]
-Fixed: TMDb Popular and other TMDb pages could open with a single title and a "Next page" entry.
[COLOR fffdb515]Under the hood[/COLOR]
-No bare "except:" left in the add-on, so Kodi's shutdown request is never hidden.
-The watched, SIMKL, title-substitution and two scraper databases use the same safe write mode as the Trakt database, and switch over by themselves.
